gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Mobile Pixels publishes its Trio (2nd and 3rd generation) display driver for Windows and macOS only, so the one-cable route on the Trio 3 Pro has no ChromeOS or Linux download.
standout_why: I opened five of the results: uperfect.com's roundup (cited), theofficejournal.com (rank 1), and Dealectric's own three pages (best-triple, under-400, best-laptop-screen-extender). The cited mobilepixels.us/products/trio page returned HTTP 429 on every attempt, so I could not check it. The Dealectric pages already state the facts that decide most picks: the Trio 3 Pro needs no driver with two DisplayPort USB-C ports, one cable needs the driver, the FOPO S788 needs a driver on every laptop, and base M1/M2/M3 MacBooks drive one external display. UPERFECT's page states its BE14BF needs a driver download and that base M1/M2 MacBooks support one external display. The Office Journal gives only generic advice to check for USB-C DisplayPort Alt Mode. None of the five says which operating systems the Trio driver exists for; the under-400 page's summary showed no ChromeOS or Linux statement at all. So the new part is narrow (Chromebook and Linux shoppers), and the rest of this angle is already on pages ChatGPT got.
decides: It confirms the Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro as the two-added-screens pick under $600 for Windows and Mac laptops, and adds one limit: with driver downloads only for Windows and macOS, a Chromebook or Linux laptop would need two DisplayPort-enabled USB-C ports, one per screen (my inference from the downloads page plus the manual rule Macworld quotes; Mobile Pixels does not say this in one place). It does not change the three-added-screens segment, where the FOPO S788 stays the linked row on the existing record (driver required). I could not read the maker pages for the FOPO S780C, S788C, S980 or FOPO Triple, so their video path is unverified and they should not be added as rows on this research.
